notes: This contract selects the 2025 Requirements Lab restore-control requirements exercised by Umbra's embedded development profile. It covers an accepted restore request, all-member initiation, the normally returned request/confirmation boundary, Federate Restore Complete's true/false C++ selectors, post-save state rollback, completion/failure/abort callbacks, status reporting, and a bounded resignation/failure boundary. The HLA_EVOKED restore-resignation lane proves that a resigning participant invalidates its in-flight restore, leaves the Federation Restored failure to surviving members, and clears the departing ambassador's queued restore callbacks before the next evoke. It does not establish complete role churn, durable snapshot serialization, or delivery of stale callback work after resignation. The contract also covers eight lifetime/state regressions: restoring a saved temporal image must not let a post-save MessageRetractionHandle alias fresh post-restore traffic; must restore a pre-save live TSO interaction payload plus its recipient ledger after a post-save Retract made that record terminal; must preserve pre-save terminal interaction, timestamped-attribute, and timestamped-object-deletion tombstones as MessageCanNoLongerBeRetracted rather than invalid handles; must restore saved logical time and actual lookahead after post-save mutations; must retain a saved deferred lookahead-decrease target so the restored time window follows the same later grant behavior; must reconstitute a saved, still-pending Non-Regulated-Grant Time Advance Request with a fresh stale-work-fenced callback after Federation Restored under both HLA_EVOKED and HLA_IMMEDIATE; must reconstitute a single-member pending Flush Queue Request under both callback models so a fresh Flush Queue Grant follows Federation Restored; and must reconstitute single-federate pending TARA, NMR, and NMRA requests in both callback models so fresh Time Advance Grants follow Federation Restored. A new three-member companion restores one queued timestamped attribute passel for two constrained recipients and proves each recipient's independent Flush Queue delivery and post-delivery Request Retraction. A one-member terminal-attribute companion preserves a saved MessageCanNoLongerBeRetracted tombstone while rejecting a post-save handle discarded by restore. A one-member terminal-deletion companion also restores the released object/name state and rejects a distinct post-save deletion handle. A timed save/restore companion now retains a timestamp-eight default-source attribute passel across a timestamp-six admission boundary before restoring it for FQR reflection and Request Retraction; RL-141 records the cross-service boundary relation. The focused filesystem lane also proves the per-joined-federate report sequence continues across the restored application snapshot. It explicitly does not claim complete HLA save/restore semantics, multi-member pending/in-transit advance restoration, queued/in-transit TSO beyond these bounded cases, durable external persistence, general timed restore, general post-restore handle remapping, transport, protected review, package support, or conformance.

requirements.notes: The bounded three-member image restores one queued timestamped Update Attribute Values passel with two constrained recipients. Each restored recipient independently reaches Flush Queue delivery, retains the original payload and retraction metadata, and receives Request Retraction after the producer retracts the restored live designator. This is not multi-member pending/in-transit advance restoration or durable recovery.
